correctness.rationale: For m=3, explicit 4-decimations close on the odd-part sequence, its backward shift, and fixed automatic decimations of t_3 modulo 2^s. For m=5 and m=9, the published exact valuation formulas justify integral normalization of the published block recurrences, yielding fixed recurrences Y_r=5Y_{r-2}-4Y_{r-4} and Y_r=205Y_{r-2}-8274Y_{r-4}+68224Y_{r-6}-65536Y_{r-8}. Companion-matrix powers modulo 2^s are eventually periodic in a finite matrix monoid, while the finitely many initial normalized slices are automatic. Exact finite computation independently checks the identities and recurrences through coefficient index 200000.

originality.rationale: Shen's September 2026 paper states all-exponent odd-part automaticity as Conjecture 6.1 and proves other exponent families, while explicitly leaving m=3 within the conjecture. The June Shen-Wang paper proves valuations for m=5 and m=9 but does not state odd-part automaticity in its accessible full text. Equivalent-formulation searches did not locate prior coverage. Xinping Wang's May 2026 undergraduate thesis was not fully inspected and remains the principal residual source-access risk; the recency of the conjecture paper also leaves concurrent-work risk.

value.rationale: The result settles three nontrivial cases of a newly stated conjecture, including a case with zeros and two cases with unbounded valuation depth. It also extracts a reusable finite-recurrence mechanism for converting exact 2-adic valuation formulas into automatic odd parts. Together with previously known cases, only m=7 remains unresolved among exponents at most 9.
